historical_references.reference: Al-Namiq (The Grilled) is a name given to Iblis (Satan) in Islamic tradition, referring to his refusal to prostrate before Adam. This event took place during the creation of mankind, making it one of the earliest references in Islamic history.

The term Al-Namiq is also used in Sufi literature to describe a seeker who, in his spiritual journey, has passed beyond the initial stages of faith and is now subjected to trials and tribulations, much like the trial of Iblis. This interpretation is rooted in the rich mystical tradition of Sufism within Islam.
